J, 02/25/2022), requires that all product discovered [redacted] s nonconforming will be documented in a nonconformance log and either on a paper record ( [redacted] ™) or electronically through a [redacted]. Your firm manufactures the SAM Model 9-10000 Sleep Apnea Recorder (K240100, MNR), which is intended to be used as an aid that records airflow, breathing effort, and body position for diagnostic evaluation ofpatients using quantitative and qualitative analysis. Your firm identified [redacted] units since [redacted] of the Class II SAM Model 9-10000 Sleep Apnea Recorder as nonconforming product due to an effort sensor failure and documented them in the nonconformance log with no additional evaluation documented on a [redacted] record or in the [redacted]. The establishment failed to ensure donors are in good health prior to donation. Specifically, donors are not systematically evaluated for pulse regularity at each donation. During the inspection, review of the following revealed this deficiency: e Your firm’s procedures include provisions for consulting the medical staff when an irregular pulse is identified; however, operations have not been designed to systematically evaluate pulse regularity that would trigger such consultation. e On March 11, 2026, direct observation of donor pre-donation physical examinations showed screening staff used the [redacted] to screen pulse, blood pressure, and temperature, but did not manually palpate the donor's pulse at the wrist, neck, or auscultate heart sounds to assess pulse regularity. e Review of the [redacted] () confirmed the device is not FDA cleared to detect pulse rhythm irregularities. e Procedures that include steps to evaluate a donor for an irregular pulse are not being followed. Specifically, Standard Operating Procedure TOOL-219398, "Donor Screening Job Aid," Version 8.0, states pulse regularity should be checked after being referred to the center medical personnel when initial pulse readings are out of range. Review of donation records for 8 out of 8 donors with out-of-range pulse readings who were referred to the center's physician substitute showed that the [redacted] re-take of the donor's pulse was not performed by the MSS, which would indicate these donors were not screened for an irregular pulse. In one case, Donor [redacted] ()(7XC) was found to have an out-of-range pulse on [redacted] of “tie” visits and was referred to the physician substitute. This donor's pulse was never taken a third time by medical staff. In all cases, donors were not allowed to donate because the pulse was found to be out of range. Your firm collected Source Plasma from [redacted] donors in 2024, [redacted] donors in 2025, and [redacted] donors in 2026 (year-to-date).
